children.text: sarveṣāṃ bhāvānāṃ sarvatra na vidyate svabhāvaścet /
children.translated_text: If the <s>svabhāva</s> (inherent nature) of all entities does not exist anywhere,
then your statement, being without <s>svabhāva</s>, is unable to negate inherent nature. [Vv 1]

children.text: atha sasvabhāvametadvākyaṃ śrutvā hatā pratijñā te /
children.translated_text: If, upon hearing this, this statement of yours possesses <s>svabhāva</s>, then your thesis is defeated;
there is an inconsistency in that, and a special reason must be stated [for the exception]. [Vv 2]
You might think: 'Let it be like sound' — but this is not tenable,
for the prevention of that [inherent nature] is [accomplished] here by sound, which exists. [Vv 3]
If you hold that 'the negation too is negated in the same way,' that is simply wrong;

children.text: evaṃ tava pratijñā lakṣaṇato duṣyate na mama || 4 ||
children.translated_text: thus your thesis is vitiated by its own defining characteristic, not mine. [Vv 4]

children.text: pratyakṣeṇa hi tāvan yadyupalabhya vinivartayasi bhāvān /
children.translated_text: If you negate entities by first apprehending them through direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>),
then that direct perception by which entities are apprehended does not exist. [Vv 5]
Inference (<s>anumāna</s>) is refuted along with direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), and scripture (<s>āgama</s>) and analogy (<s>upamāna</s>) likewise;
and those objects established by inference, scripture, and example [are also refuted]. [Vv 6]
Those who know the states of <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) hold that wholesome <s>dharmas</s>
have a wholesome nature inherently; the same application holds for the remaining [categories] too. [Vv 7]
The nature of <s>dharmas</s> leading to final liberation (<s>nairyāṇika</s>) is that which leads to liberation, and for those
whose states of <s>dharma</s> have been declared — likewise for those leading to liberation and the rest. [Vv 8]

children.text: yadi ca na bhavet svabhāvo dharmāṇāṃ niḥsvabhāva ityevam /
children.translated_text: And if the <s>svabhāva</s> of <s>dharmas</s> does not exist, then the very term
'without inherent nature' (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>) would not exist either, for even a name does not exist without a referent. [Vv 9]

children.text: atha vidyate svabhāvaḥ sa ca dharmāṇāṃ na vidyate tasmāt /
children.translated_text: If, on the other hand, <s>svabhāva</s> exists, but it does not belong to <s>dharmas</s>, then

children.text: dharmairvinā svabhāvaḥ sa yasyāsti tad yuktamupadeṣṭum || 10 ||
children.translated_text: it is proper to teach that <s>svabhāva</s> exists without <s>dharmas</s> — whose [nature] is that? [Vv 10]

children.text: sata eva pratiṣedho nāsti ghaṭo geha ityayaṃ yasmāt /
children.translated_text: Negation is only of something that exists — since [one says] 'there is no pot in the house,'

children.text: dṛṣṭaḥ pratiṣedho 'yaṃ sataḥ svabhāvasya te tasmāt || 11 ||
children.translated_text: this negation is observed [to be] of an existent; therefore your [negation] is of an existent <s>svabhāva</s>. [Vv 11]

children.text: atha nāsti sa svabhāvaḥ kiṃ nu pratividhyate tvayānena /
children.translated_text: If that <s>svabhāva</s> does not exist, then what exactly is being negated by you
with this statement? For negation of a non-existent is established even without a statement. [Vv 12]
Just as the grasping of water in a mirage is false, as if by children,
so too would your false grasping be, since you are negating what is non-existent. [Vv 13]

children.text: nanvevaṃ satyasti grāho grāhyaṃ ca tagdṛhītaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Indeed, if it is so, then there exists a grasping, a graspable, and a grasped,

children.text: pratiṣedhaḥ pratiṣedhyaṃ pratiṣeddhā ceti ṣaṭkaṃ tat || 14 ||
children.translated_text: and a negation, a negandum, and a negator — that makes a set of six. [Vv 14]

children.text: atha naivāsti grāho na ca grāhyaṃ na ca grahītāraḥ /
children.translated_text: But if there is no grasping, no graspable, and no graspers,

children.text: pratiṣedhaḥ pratiṣedhyaṃ pratiṣeddhāro 'sya tu na santi || 15 ||
children.translated_text: then there is no negation, no negandum, and no negators of this. [Vv 15]

children.text: pratiṣedhaḥ pratiṣedhyaṃ pratiṣeddhāraśca yadyuta na santi /
children.translated_text: If the negation, the negandum, and the negators do not exist,
then all entities are established, and their <s>svabhāva</s> too [is established] for those [who hold this view]. [Vv 16]

children.text: hetostato na siddhirnaiḥsvābhāvyāt kuto hi te hetuḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore there is no establishment from a reason (<s>hetu</s>); for due to the absence of inherent nature, how can you have a reason?
And the establishment of your thesis without a reason is not tenable. [Vv 17]

children.text: yadi cāhetoḥ siddhiḥ svabhāvavinivartanasya te bhavati /
children.translated_text: And if the establishment of your negation of <s>svabhāva</s> is without a reason,
then the existence of inherent nature is also established for me without a reason. [Vv 18]
If the existence [comes] from a reason, then the absence of <s>svabhāva</s> of entities is untenable,

children.text: loke naiḥsvābhāvyānna hi kaścana vidyate bhāvaḥ || 19 ||
children.translated_text: for in the world, there exists no entity whatsoever that is without <s>svabhāva</s>. [Vv 19]

children.text: pūrvaṃ cet pratiṣedhaḥ paścāt pratiṣedhyamiti ca nopapannam /
children.translated_text: And [the view] that the negation comes first and the negandum after is not tenable;
coming after is untenable, as is simultaneously, because <s>svabhāva</s> is non-existent. [Vv 20]
[Response:] If, even when my statement does not [stand] apart from the aggregate of causes and conditions,
then surely emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) is established, since entities lack <s>svabhāva</s>. [Vv 21]

children.text: yaśca pratītya bhāvo bhāvānāṃ śūnyateti sā hyuktā /
children.translated_text: That entity which arises dependently — the emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) of entities is declared to be precisely that;

children.text: yaśca pratītya bhāvo bhavati hi tasyāsvabhāvatvam || 22 ||
children.translated_text: for that which arises dependently — it indeed has no <s>svabhāva</s> (inherent nature). [Vv 22]
Just as a magically created being (<s>nirmitaka</s>) might negate another magically created being
produced by a magical person (<s>māyāpuruṣa</s>) through his own illusion — this negation would be just like that. [Vv 23]
This statement is not inherently real (<s>svābhāvika</s>); therefore there is no abandonment of my thesis,

children.text: nāsti ca vaiṣamikatvaṃ viśeṣahetuśca na nigadyaḥ || 24 ||
children.translated_text: and there is no inconsistency, and no special reason needs to be stated. [Vv 24]

children.text: mā śabdavaditi nāyaṃ dṛṣṭānto yastvayā mamārabdhaḥ /
children.translated_text: The example 'let it be like sound' that you have proposed against me is not [a valid] illustration,

children.text: śabdena hi tacca śabdasya vāraṇaṃ naiva me vacaḥ || 25 ||
children.translated_text: for sound indeed prevents that [future sound], but my statement does not [work that way]. [Vv 25]
If the prevention of things without <s>svabhāva</s> is indeed by [something itself] without <s>svabhāva</s>,
then upon the cessation of the absence of <s>svabhāva</s>, <s>svabhāva</s> itself would be established. [Vv 26]
Or alternatively, just as with regard to a magically created woman, [one would not grasp] 'this is a [real] woman' —
A magically created being would refute [the objection]; for someone it would be just so. // Vv 27 //

children.text: athavā sādhyasamo 'yaṃ heturna hi vidyate dhvaneḥ sattā /
children.translated_text: Or else, this reason is equivalent to what is to be proved (<s>sādhyasama</s>), for sound has no [inherent] existence;
And we speak of conventional usage without accepting [it as ultimately real]. // Vv 28 //

children.text: yadi kācana pratijñā tatra syādeṣa me bhaveddoṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: If I had any thesis whatsoever, then this fault would apply to me;

children.text: nāsti ca mama pratijñā tasmānnaivāsti me doṣaḥ || 29 ||
children.translated_text: But I have no thesis, therefore I have no fault at all. // Vv 29 //
If I were to apprehend anything at all, I would either affirm or negate;
Since those objects [established] through perception and other [means of knowledge] do not exist [for me], there is no reproach against me. // Vv 30 //
And if the establishment of those objects is through the <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge),

children.text: teṣāṃ punaḥ prasiddhiṃ brūhi kathaṃ te pramāṇānām || 31 ||
children.translated_text: Then tell [me], how is the establishment of those <s>pramāṇas</s> themselves [achieved]? // Vv 31 //
If the establishment of the <s>pramāṇas</s> is through other <s>pramāṇas</s>, there is an infinite regress;
There is no establishment of the beginning, nor of the middle, nor of the end. // Vv 32 //
If, on the other hand, those [pramāṇas] are established without [other] <s>pramāṇas</s>, then your position is abandoned;
There is inconsistency in that, and a special reason must be stated [for the exception]. // Vv 33 //
This is an unfair comparison, for fire does not illuminate itself;
For its non-apprehension is not seen [in darkness], as [is that] of a pot in darkness. // Vv 35 //
If, according to your statement, fire illuminates itself,
Then fire will also burn itself, just as it [burns] another. // Vv 36 //
And if, according to your statement, fire illuminates both itself and others,
Then darkness too will conceal both itself and others, just as fire [illuminates]. // Vv 37 //

children.text: nāsti tamaśca jvalane yatra ca tiṣṭhati sadātmani jvalanaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no darkness in fire, nor in that [place] where fire always abides in itself;

children.text: kurute kathaṃ prakāśaṃ sa hi prakāśo 'ndhakāravadhaḥ || 38 ||
children.translated_text: How then does it produce illumination? For illumination is the destruction of darkness. // Vv 38 //
The claim that fire illuminates at the very moment of its arising is a false doctrine;

children.text: utpadyamāna eva prāpnoti tamo na hi hutāśaḥ || 39 ||
children.translated_text: For fire, at the very moment of arising, does not reach darkness. // Vv 39 //
If fire could destroy darkness even without reaching it,
Then fire situated here would destroy the darkness in all world-realms. // Vv 40 //
And if the establishment of <s>pramāṇas</s> is self-sufficient (<s>svataḥ</s>), not depending on the objects to be known (<s>prameyas</s>),
Then the establishment of <s>pramāṇas</s> is independent of anything else — for establishment [in that case] does not depend on another. // Vv 41 //

children.text: anapekṣya hi prameyānarthān yadi te pramāṇasiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: If the establishment of your <s>pramāṇas</s> is independent of the objects to be known,
Then these <s>pramāṇas</s> are not the <s>pramāṇas</s> of anything whatsoever. // Vv 42 //
Now, if you hold that their establishment is in dependence [on prameyas], what is the fault in that?
It would be the proving of what is already proved, for what is [already] established does not depend on another. // Vv 43 //

children.text: sidhyanti hi prameyāṇyapekṣya yadi sarvathā pramāṇāni /
children.translated_text: If the objects to be known (<s>prameyas</s>) are in all cases established in dependence on <s>pramāṇas</s>,
Then the establishment of <s>prameyas</s> would be independent of <s>pramāṇas</s> [after all]. // Vv 44 //
And if the establishment of <s>prameyas</s> is indeed independent of <s>pramāṇas</s>,

children.text: kiṃ te pramāṇasiddhyā tāni yadarthaṃ prasiddhaṃ tat || 45 ||
children.translated_text: What is the point of establishing <s>pramāṇas</s>? That for whose sake [they exist] is already established. // Vv 45 //
But if the establishment of <s>pramāṇas</s> depends on <s>prameyas</s>,

children.text: vyatyaya evaṃ sati te dhruvaṃ pramāṇaprameyāṇām || 46 ||
children.translated_text: Then there is certainly a reversal of [the relationship between] your <s>pramāṇas</s> and <s>prameyas</s>. // Vv 46 //

body.text: atha tai pramāṇasiddhyā prameyasiddhiḥ prameyasiddhyā cā

children.translated_text: There is the establishment of <s>pramāṇas</s>, then neither of the two is established for you. // Vv 47 //

body.translated_text: If through the establishment of <s>pramāṇas</s> there is the establishment of <s>prameyas</s>, and through the establishment of <s>prameyas</s>

children.text: sidhyanti hi pramāṇairyadi prameyāṇi tāni taireva /
children.translated_text: If <s>prameyas</s> are established by <s>pramāṇas</s>, and those very [pramāṇas]
Are to be established by <s>prameyas</s>, how will they establish [them]? // Vv 48 //

children.text: sidhyanti ca prameyairyadi pramāṇāni tāni taireva /
children.translated_text: And if <s>pramāṇas</s> are established by <s>prameyas</s>, and those very [prameyas]
Are to be established by <s>pramāṇas</s>, how will they establish [them]? // Vv 49 //

children.text: pitrā yadyutpādyaḥ putro yadi tena caiva putreṇa /
children.translated_text: If a son is to be produced by a father, and if by that very son

children.text: utpādyaḥ sa yadi pitā vada tatrotpādayati kaḥ kam || 50 ||
children.translated_text: That father is to be produced, then tell me — in that case, who produces whom? // Vv 50 //

children.text: kaśca pitā kaḥ putrastatra tvaṃ brūhi tāvubhāvapi ca /
children.translated_text: And who is the father and who is the son there? Tell me — for both of them
Bear the characteristics of father and son, and hence our doubt [remains]. // Vv 51 //
The establishment of <s>pramāṇas</s> is neither self-established, nor through each other, nor through [other] <s>pramāṇas</s>,

children.text: bhavati na ca prameyairna cāpyakasmāt pramāṇānām || 52 ||
children.translated_text: Nor through <s>prameyas</s>, nor without any cause at all. // Vv 52 //
Those who speak of the nature of wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>) <s>dharmas</s> as [having] a fixed state of nature (<s>dharmāvasthā</s>),
Should be described as [asserting] wholesome intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) through such classification. // Vv 53 //

children.text: yadi ca pratītya kuśalaḥ svabhāva utpadyate sa kuśalānām /
children.translated_text: And if the intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) of wholesome [dharmas] arises dependently,

children.text: dharmāṇāṃ parabhāvaḥ svabhāva evaṃ kathaṃ bhavati || 54 ||
children.translated_text: Then that would be the other-nature (<s>parabhāva</s>) of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> — how then can it be intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>)? // Vv 54 //

children.text: atha na pratītya kiṃcit svabhāva utpadyate sa kuśalānām /
children.translated_text: Now, if without dependence [on conditions], <s>svabhāva</s> (inherent nature) arises independently, then for wholesome
<s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) it would be thus — there would be no dwelling in the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>). [Vv 55]

children.text: nādharmo dharmo vā saṃvyavahārāśca laukikā na syuḥ /
children.translated_text: There would be no unwholesome (<s>adharma</s>) or wholesome (<s>dharma</s>), and worldly conventions (<s>saṃvyavahāra</s>) would not exist;
all entities would be eternal, for being eternal they would be without cause. [Vv 56]
And this fault applies to unwholesome, indeterminate, and <s>nairyāṇika</s> (liberating) [dharmas] as well;
therefore, for you, everything conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) and unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>) becomes thus. [Vv 57]

children.text: yaḥ sadbhūtaṃ nāma brūyāt sa svabhāva ityevam /
children.translated_text: If one says that what truly exists is a name, and that is <s>svabhāva</s> — in that case,

children.text: bhavatā prativaktavyo nāma brūmaśca na vyaṃ sat || 58 ||
children.translated_text: you must reply: we do not declare a name to be existent. [Vv 58]

children.text: nāmāsaditi ca yadidaṃ tatkiṃ nu sato bhavatyutāsataḥ /
children.translated_text: And if you say 'a name is non-existent' — does it then belong to the existent or to the non-existent?

children.text: yadi hi sato yadyasato dvidhāpi te hīyate vādaḥ || 59 ||
children.translated_text: For whether it belongs to the existent or the non-existent, in both ways your argument is defeated. [Vv 59]
The emptiness (<s>śūnyatva</s>) of all entities has previously been established;
therefore this objection against [my] thesis is [itself] a fault. [Vv 60]

children.text: atha vidyate svabhāvaḥ sa ca dharmāṇāṃ na vidyata iti /
children.translated_text: Now, if <s>svabhāva</s> exists but does not belong to <s>dharmas</s> —
this suspicion that has been raised — it becomes groundless. [Vv 61]

children.text: sata eva pratiṣedho yadi śūnyatvaṃ nanvapratiṣiddhamidam /
children.translated_text: If negation is only of an existent, and emptiness [would mean] the non-negated still remains,
then you are [in fact] negating the absence of <s>svabhāva</s> (<s>niḥsvabhāvatva</s>) of entities. [Vv 62]

children.text: pratiṣedhayase 'tha tvaṃ śūnyatvaṃ tacca nāsti śūnyatvam /
children.translated_text: If, on the other hand, you negate emptiness (<s>śūnyatva</s>), and that emptiness does not exist —

children.text: pratiṣedhaḥ sata iti te nanvevaṃ hīyate vādaḥ || 63 ||
children.translated_text: then your [position] that 'negation is of an existent' — is not your argument thereby defeated? [Vv 63]

children.text: pratiṣedhayāmi nāhaṃ kiṃcit pratiṣedhyamasti na ca kiṃcit /
children.translated_text: I do not negate anything, and there is nothing to be negated;
therefore, your [accusation] 'you negate' is an utterly false imputation. [Vv 64]
And as to your [claim that] from my statement 'the negating statement of the non-existent is established' —
here, speech indicates 'it is non-existent'; it does not destroy that [non-existent thing]. [Vv 65]
Regarding the mirage illustration: the great wonder that you have again stated —

children.text: tatrāpi nirṇayaṃ śṛṇu yathā sa dṛṣṭānta upapannaḥ || 66 ||
children.translated_text: hear the determination concerning that as well, [namely] how that illustration is valid. [Vv 66]

children.text: sa yadi svabhāvataḥ syāt bhāvo na syāt pratītyasamudbhūtaḥ /
children.translated_text: If that entity existed by <s>svabhāva</s> (own-nature), it would not arise dependently (<s>pratītyasamudbhūta</s>);

children.text: yaśca pratītya bhavati grāho nanu śūnyatā saiva || 67 ||
children.translated_text: and that which arises dependently — is not that grasping [of it as inherently real] precisely emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>)? [Vv 67]

children.text: yadi ca svabhāvataḥ syād grāhaḥ kastaṃ nivartayed grāhyam /
children.translated_text: And if grasping existed by <s>svabhāva</s>, who could avert that grasping?
The same rule applies to the remaining [cases]; therefore, the fault [you raise] is not applicable. [Vv 68]

children.text: etena hetvabhāvaḥ pratyuktaḥ pūrvameva sa samatvāt /
children.translated_text: By this, the [objection concerning] absence of a reason (<s>hetu</s>) is answered, for it was already [addressed] previously due to its being the same [type of argument]
as the one stated earlier in the procedure of refuting the mirage illustration. [Vv 69]

children.text: yastraikālye hetuḥ pratyuktaḥ pūrvameva sa samatvāt /
children.translated_text: The reason [concerning] the three times — it was already answered previously due to its being the same;
and the counter-reason regarding the three times is [also] available to the proponents of emptiness (<s>śūnyatāvādin</s>). [Vv 70]

children.text: prabhavati ca śūnyateyaṃ yasya prabhavanti tasya sarvārthāḥ /
children.translated_text: For one for whom this emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) is viable, all things (<s>artha</s>) become viable;

children.text: prabhavati na tasya kiṃ na bhavati śūnyatā yasyeti || 71 ||
children.translated_text: for one for whom emptiness is not viable — does anything at all become viable? [Vv 71]
[<s>Nāgārjuna</s>] who taught emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), the middle path (<s>madhyamā pratipad</s>), as having multiple meanings —
I bow to that matchless Fully Awakened One (<s>Saṃbuddha</s>). [Vv 72]
